what_good_looks_like: a first-time visitor can restate who it is for and the outcome within one screen
what_bad_looks_like: hero leads with the company name or a vague slogan and states no outcome
signal_to_check: H1 + subhead + hero copy above the fold
white_space_test: every competitor names a feature but none names the buyer outcome

what_good_looks_like: the target buyer is named or unmistakably implied in the first section
what_bad_looks_like: copy tries to speak to everyone so it lands with no one
signal_to_check: hero and first-section language; use-case or industry callouts
white_space_test: all rivals stay generic and a named niche is unclaimed

what_good_looks_like: states a specific reason to choose it over the obvious alternative
what_bad_looks_like: claims any competitor could copy verbatim (fast; easy; trusted)
signal_to_check: why-us or comparison copy; specificity of the claims made
white_space_test: the whole set makes interchangeable claims

what_good_looks_like: the eye lands on the primary action first with a clear size and weight order
what_bad_looks_like: competing focal points so everything shouts and nothing reads
signal_to_check: headline-vs-body contrast; CTA prominence; first-screen scan path
white_space_test: no competitor has a calm confident first screen

what_good_looks_like: a deliberate type pairing with a consistent scale and reading rhythm
what_bad_looks_like: system-default fonts; inconsistent sizes; cramped line length
signal_to_check: heading and body fonts; scale steps; measure and line-height
white_space_test: the niche relies on default system fonts

what_good_looks_like: a restrained palette used consistently with accessible text contrast
what_bad_looks_like: many unrelated hues; low-contrast text; no repeated accent
signal_to_check: count of distinct hues; text-on-background contrast; accent reuse
white_space_test: no competitor owns a distinct memorable color

what_good_looks_like: claims are backed by numbers cases or named concrete detail
what_bad_looks_like: adjectives without evidence and stock superlatives
signal_to_check: presence of metrics; case detail; named examples
white_space_test: rivals assert quality but none proves it

what_good_looks_like: recent updates dated content or a maintained resource section
what_bad_looks_like: stale copyright year; dead blog; abandoned resources
signal_to_check: footer year; latest post date; changelog or news section
white_space_test: the niche looks dormant so recency is unclaimed

what_good_looks_like: labels and nav predict where content lives so users find it fast
what_bad_looks_like: clever-but-opaque labels; buried key pages; weak navigation
signal_to_check: nav labels; page titles; link-text clarity
white_space_test: no competitor makes core answers easy to reach

what_good_looks_like: specific testimonials logos or counts placed near the decision points
what_bad_looks_like: no proof or vague unattributed quotes
signal_to_check: testimonial attribution; client logos; review counts
white_space_test: the set shows little credible social proof

what_good_looks_like: team faces credentials guarantees or third-party validation are visible
what_bad_looks_like: an anonymous faceless site with no accountability signals
signal_to_check: about or team page; certifications; guarantees
white_space_test: no competitor shows the humans behind the work

what_good_looks_like: pricing contact and policies are easy to find and plainly stated
what_bad_looks_like: hidden pricing; contact buried; evasive policy language
signal_to_check: pricing page; contact visibility; policy clarity
white_space_test: the niche hides pricing so openness becomes a wedge

what_good_looks_like: one dominant action per view with an outcome-oriented label
what_bad_looks_like: many equal CTAs or generic submit and learn-more labels
signal_to_check: count of primary buttons above the fold; label wording
white_space_test: every rival buries or clutters its main action

what_good_looks_like: the path to act is short and forms ask only what is needed
what_bad_looks_like: long forms; forced signup; needless steps before any value
signal_to_check: form field count; steps to convert; gates placed before value
white_space_test: competitors gate everything so a low-friction path wins

what_good_looks_like: legible type reachable CTA and comfortable tap targets on a phone
what_bad_looks_like: desktop-only layout; tiny taps; CTA pushed off-screen on mobile
signal_to_check: responsive layout; tap-target size; mobile CTA placement

what_good_looks_like: titles headings and copy target the real language buyers search
what_bad_looks_like: keyword-thin or keyword-stuffed; missing H1; jargon-only copy
signal_to_check: title tag; H1 and H2 terms; body keyword relevance
white_space_test: no competitor speaks the searcher's actual words

what_good_looks_like: clean meta descriptions and relevant structured data are present
what_bad_looks_like: missing or duplicate meta; no schema; poor share previews
signal_to_check: meta description; JSON-LD presence; open-graph tags
white_space_test: rivals ignore structured data and share previews

what_good_looks_like: fast first paint stable layout and lightweight hero media
what_bad_looks_like: heavy unoptimized media; visible layout shift; slow first screen
signal_to_check: hero asset weight; render-blocking resources; layout shift
white_space_test: the niche is slow so speed is an easy differentiator
